declared.title: Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis
declared.foundIn: nommée dans la consigne de la session ; titre relevé sur la recherche Crossref « choice overload meta-analysis » du 2026-11-22 (Crossref y donne 2014, la revue 2015) : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: 99 observations from earlier experiments on assortment size (N = 7,202); countries not given in the abstract

findings.text: Many options hurt more when the options are complex, the task is hard, people do not know what they prefer, and they want to decide with little effort

support.sentence: We further show that each of these four factors has a reliable and significant impact on choice overload, whereby higher levels of decision task difficulty, greater choice set complexity, higher preference uncertainty, and a more prominent, effort-minimizing goal facilitate choice overload.

findings.text: Once the four factors are in the model, the overall effect of assortment size on choice overload is statistically significant; the abstract gives no size

support.sentence: Finally, we document that when moderating variables are taken into account the overall effect of assortment size on choice overload is significant-a finding counter to the data reported by prior meta-analytic research.

limits: the four conditions are coded across studies, never manipulated together in one experiment
consumer choices; samples' countries not given in the abstract
corrigendum 10.1016/j.jcps.2015.07.001, not linked by Crossref: the mean-effect section has b = .17 and .41 (p < .001) but also b = .04 (p > .4)
which corrected coefficient is the effect without moderators is not read (closed text): read as a conditional effect, not as an average
the effect varies strongly by outcome measure (mcshane-2018-multilevel, co-authored by Böckenholt)
